name: Headline assembles inside a halo of syntax chips
looks: A serif word types in, settles, and a second italic word lands beneath it in the accent colour with a blinking cursor. Small torn-paper chips (each naming a tiny syntax feature) pop in around the headline at scattered angles, each connected to the centre by a thin straight line.
build: The headline uses terminal-type-on's per-character reveal in a serif face; the chips use annotated-diagram-overlay's label-and-leader-line mechanic, but radiating outward from the headline instead of pointing at a single spot, each chip's line revealed with strokeDashoffset as it lands, staggered 0.1-0.15s apart.
sound: A soft typewriter clack under the headline, then a light pop per chip landing.
prompt: Introduce a text-editing product by typing its core verb on screen, then surround the headline with a small halo of torn-paper chips, each naming one tiny feature and connected back to the headline by a thin line, so the breadth of what it does reads at a glance.
